entries.title: Designed the engineering-reflection skill
entries.summary: Iterated a text-only reflection skill into a cumulative visual roadmap (git-tree HTML) with an inclusion gate so only real learning gets recorded.

tradeoffs.chosen: Inclusion gate: record only genuine learning or debated trade-offs
tradeoffs.rejected: Log every session as a node
tradeoffs.why: You raised this directly — the roadmap should map the learning curve, not activity; mechanical work (downloads, renames) shouldn't clutter it.

bugs.symptom: Script crashed: Cannot access 'typeOf' before initialization
bugs.rootCause: render() ran before const TYPES/typeOf/CSS were initialized — only function declarations hoist, not const (temporal dead zone).
bugs.fix: Moved the persist+render call to the end of the file, after all const declarations.

learnings: The roadmap should map the learning curve, not activity — only genuine questions/debates earn a node.
A trade-off is only worth recording if it was actually debated; a bug the agent fixes alone is low-signal.
entries.impact: Turned a throwaway text summary into a durable, growing visual record of how the project's thinking evolves.

entries.title: SkillGuard architecture grill + engine-only PRD
entries.summary: Grilled a one-paragraph 'AI security for skills' idea into a decision-complete architecture (glossary, 2 ADRs, PRD, GitHub issue), walking a design tree one dependency at a time and isolating the single unproven risk into a shippable first slice.

tradeoffs.rejected: Chrome Extension or GitHub Actions interception
tradeoffs.why: The extension only catches browser-discovered skills and CI only catches repo-committed ones; the CLI gate sits at the one choke point every install path (clone/curl/zip) converges on, and stays agent-agnostic so browser/CI become later clients not rewrites.

tradeoffs.chosen: Hash-first, upload-on-miss with a shared verdict cache
tradeoffs.rejected: Always upload full content, or scan fully locally
tradeoffs.why: Always-upload leaks content even for already-known skills; fully-local kills the shared cache and forces a weak on-device model. Hash-first keeps known skills private AND builds a network-effect cache where one scan protects every later developer.

tradeoffs.chosen: Canonical bundle hash (LF-normalized, junk-excluded) as skill identity
tradeoffs.why: User stress-tested with 'two devs download the same skill — same hash?': raw bytes diverge on Windows CRLF vs Linux LF (near-zero cache hits), source+version misses forks/mirrors. Only content-addressed + canonicalized identity makes 'same skill -> same hash' hold cross-platform, which the whole moat depends on.

tradeoffs.chosen: Hybrid static + LLM detection with defense-in-depth
tradeoffs.why: Static alone misses semantic injection ('review env config files' with no banned keyword); LLM alone is costly and can be prompt-injected by the skill it reads. Hybrid pairs a deterministic static floor the LLM can't downgrade with semantic judgment that only ever escalates.

tradeoffs.rejected: Build full v1 (gate + cache + DB + provenance) up front
tradeoffs.why: Detection quality is the sole unproven risk; everything else is known plumbing. Validating the engine against an eval corpus before wrapping infra around it avoids betting plumbing on an engine that might not work.

learnings: An install-time CLI gate is the universal choke point for AI-skill installs, because every discovery path still has to land the skill on disk before the agent trusts it.
A shared verdict cache only works if identity is content-addressed AND canonicalized (LF line endings, exclude .git/OS junk) so the same skill yields the same hash across Windows/Mac/Linux.
Static detection is grep-on-steroids for known-bad primitives (curl|bash, ~/.ssh, base64 -d | sh) but is blind to innocent-sounding semantic injection, which is what the LLM layer is for.

A security analyzer's input is adversarial toward the analyzer itself: a skill can try to talk the LLM into a CLEAN verdict, so manipulation attempts must escalate the verdict, backed by a static floor the LLM can never downgrade.
entries.impact: Converted a vague product idea into a documented, testable architecture that de-risks the one uncertain component first, demonstrating design judgment under adversarial security constraints.
